differences.reason: Evolution throws a BigInteger overflow and fails to complete simulation.
Evolution leaves the Reptar Local Bus unsimulated.
Evolution requires QuestaSim to simulate a VHDL entity. Under the maintainer's November 7, 2026 decision, QuestaSim is out of scope and Mobile simulates through the companion.
With a HIGH trigger and error inputs, Evolution opens a dialog that fails in headless mode.
The fixture changes a width without supplying table rows. Both programs open the PLA as 2×2, which makes the probe points incompatible.
With seed 0 and Evolution appearances, Evolution uses System.currentTimeMillis() and Mobile uses deterministic seeding.
Evolution times the 74123 pulse with System.nanoTime() and Mobile uses simulated time.

These rows date to 51b03c89 and 72b6bae3, when Mobile co-simulated BLIF through the companion. Since #335, Mobile simulates BLIF the same way as Evolution. The blif-circuit evidence reruns these suites for BLIF alone and compares the results with Evolution.
Evolution cannot resave the BLIF truth table in headless mode because the parse error opens a dialog. The corpus suites compare the same fixture in settle and step modes.

out_of_scope.reason: The maintainer excludes the Quartus, Vivado, and ISE toolchains.
The maintainer excludes physical board programming.
The maintainer's November 7, 2026 decision excludes desktop windows, Swing, Java2D, and desktop paths because they do not apply to Mobile.
The maintainer's November 7, 2026 decision excludes the licensed QuestaSim tool alongside Quartus, Vivado, and ISE.

Base/Image.FACTORY.note: Geometry, RGBA pixels, and attributes match. Evolution reopens and saves the file without loss. The original size, optimize, and transparent background menu items produce the same attributes and pixels.

Base/MenuTool.difference: The menu includes entries from MenuTool and every reachable MenuExtender for components, memory, PLA, splitters, subcircuits, SoC CPUs with and without a program, buses, PIO, VGA, PLA ROM, and Image, plus selection actions. A blank canvas opens no menu. On a wire, Mobile offers Delete and Split wire, with no wire attribute sheet. It shows the tooltip at the top of the menu because touch has no hover. Edit Contents and Edit PLA Program open the memory editor and inspector. The SoC windows for the assembler, program, memory map, and transactions appear as sections of the SoC tool. On Android, PNGs saved through the Image menu lose the RGB values of fully transparent pixels. ProgrammableGenerator is outside the Evolution d58a61e0 library and has no menu.
Base/MenuTool.note: Model oracles compared MenuDesktopOracle with ComponentMenu, including CPUs after loading ELF, and ImageMenuDesktopOracle with ImageMenu, with identical pixels. Canvas menus were exercised on iOS (CanvasPokeAndMenuTest) and in the Android emulator (#347).

Base/PokeTool.note: Pin.PinPoker.handleBitPress targets the bit or hex/octal digit under the pointer and cycles tri-state values U→0→1→U. The model oracle, PinPokeEditorTest, iOS CanvasPokeAndMenuTest, and Android touch covered this behavior. Decimal and floating-point radices open the value editor.

Base/Text.FACTORY.note: Geometry and attributes match. Evolution reopens and saves the file without loss.

Base/TextTool.note: TextTool.editingStopped covers new text, labels, edits, and empty text. Text with no explicit font uses SansSerif bold 16 (plain 12 in 2.7.1 projects) and leaves the font implicit when saved. Clearing an existing Text keeps it in the circuit, as in Evolution.

FPArithmetic/FpConstant.note: Value and geometry for each floating-point width.

I/O/Button.note: I/O oracle covers geometry in 4 directions.

I/O/DipSwitch.note: I/O oracle covers geometry with 1, 8, and 32 switches.

I/O/DotMatrix.note: I/O oracle covers geometry in column, row, and select modes and compares matrix state.

I/O/HexDigit.note: I/O oracle covers geometry with and without the decimal point. The SAP-1 corpus includes 2 displays.

I/O/Joystick.note: I/O oracle covers geometry with 2 and 5 bits.

I/O/Led.note: I/O oracle covers geometry in 4 directions.

I/O/LedBar.note: I/O oracle covers geometry in row and column modes.

I/O/RealTimeClock.note: Evolution reads ZonedDateTime.now(). Readings from both implementations fall within the same wall-clock window in milliseconds and seconds.

I/O/RgbLed.note: I/O oracle covers geometry in 4 directions.

I/O/SevenSegment.note: I/O oracle covers geometry with separate inputs and a bus input, with and without the decimal point.

I/O/Tty.note: I/O oracle covers geometry from 1×1 to 48×120 and compares TTY state.

I/O/Video.factory.note: Pixels and cursor registers match in all 10 color formats and both reset modes. The comparison excludes cursor blinking, which follows the wall clock.

Input/Output-Extra/Buzzer.difference: With a smoothed non-sinusoidal waveform and 4 × cycle < 2 × smoothing width at high frequencies, the Evolution audio thread throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException and goes silent. Mobile plays the unsmoothed waveform. At zero volume, Evolution loops a clip of zeros and Mobile skips playback. Both produce silence.
Input/Output-Extra/Buzzer.note: Tone fields across 20,000 states and PCM samples from Evolution's audio thread. For noise, the comparison covers only the fields.

Input/Output-Extra/DigitalOscilloscope.note: Trace, captured cells, and clock counter at each step, with undefined and error inputs.

Input/Output-Extra/Slider.note: The BFH/I/O-Extra oracle compares outputs bit by bit.

Input/Output-Extra/TwoPinLed.note: The BFH/I/O-Extra oracle compares outputs bit by bit.

MenuEdit/addCtrl.difference: Add vertex appends the point at the end of the polygon. To place the point in the middle of a different edge, edit the coordinates. The resulting document matches Evolution.

MenuEdit/delete.note: Portuguese labels Delete "Apagar" everywhere, as Evolution's gui_pt editClearItem, compDeleteItem and selDeleteItem (W2-09).

MenuEdit/dup.note: Mobile places the copy at the touch point. Evolution uses the pointer or the first available offset.

MenuFile/close.difference: Mobile saves the workspace draft before closing. Evolution asks whether to save when the project has unsaved changes.

MenuFile/newi.note: For a new project without a user template, libraries, toolbar, mouse mappings, and 1 Hz frequency match default.templ. As in the template, #HDL-IP starts unloaded. The library manager can add it.

MenuFile/prefs.difference: Mobile opens its own preferences panel. Each preference is compared in its own row.

MenuFile/print.difference: Mobile generates an A4 PDF with 24 pt margins and the system print dialog fits it to the paper. Evolution prints on Letter with 1-inch margins. The Mobile header uses the platform font at 12 pt and scales down if wider than the page. Evolution uses the Java default font and lets the header extend beyond the page. On the same paper, scale, rotation, position, and header text match.
MenuFile/print.note: Compared 48 pages (8 circuits, 3 headers, with and without rotation) and 60,033 header templates with Print.MyPrintable. The circuit drawing is the same as in image export.

MenuFpga/BoardEditor.note: JVM oracle (#342). BoardReaderClass reopened boards saved by Evolution and Mobile with matching describe() results and pixels for GECKO5_EDUCATION, BASYS3, and DE0_CV. Evolution's own writer changes source pixels in GECKO5_EDUCATION and BASYS3.

MenuFpga/FPGACommander.difference: Mobile names and organizes its files as logisim_fpga_top.v, pins.xdc/ucf/qsf/lpf, and a build script. Evolution uses toplevel/logisimTopLevelShell.v, circuit/, gates/, and vendor-specific scripts. Physical pins, I/O standards, pulls, and behavior at the pins match.
MenuFpga/FPGACommander.note: HDL-only generation from the saved mapping for Vivado, ISE, Quartus, and ECP5, with 128 vectors per board simulated in Icarus. The comparison excludes clocked designs, 7-segment displays, synthesis, and programming.

MenuHelp/about.difference: Mobile shows its version, build, and legal notices, including the Logisim Evolution GPL. Evolution shows its own version and credits.

MenuHelp/guide.difference: Mobile provides docs/user-guide.md and in-app guides. Evolution opens the JavaHelp guide.

MenuHelp/library.difference: Mobile shows component counts for each registered library and the matrix. Evolution opens the JavaHelp library reference.

MenuHelp/search.note: Search covers commands, components, circuits, and labels.
MenuHelp/search.difference: Mobile searches actions and the project. Evolution opens OmniSearch for menu actions.

MenuHelp/tutorial.difference: Mobile provides its own guides and examples. Evolution opens the JavaHelp tutorial.

MenuHelp/www.difference: Mobile opens its repository. Evolution opens https://github.com/logisim-evolution/.

MenuProject/addVhdl.note: Type or paste VHDL source. Simulation runs through the companion.
MenuProject/addVhdl.difference: Mobile accepts pasted VHDL text without the Evolution template. The shared definition also inserts an instance. With the same text, the document matches.

MenuProject/appearance.difference: The default drawing relative to the anchor matches. Evolution saves coordinates with an offset of 50 and uses Courier 10 Pitch. Mobile saves at the origin and uses Monospaced.

MenuProject/importVerilog.note: Three Verilog projects and 40 vectors. BLIF does not go through the Evolution importer.

MenuProject/importVhdl.note: Imports the VHDL file as a shared project definition (addSharedVhdlDefinition).

MenuProject/layout.note: Switching to the layout leaves the document unchanged in both apps.

MenuProject/loadJar.note: The companion runs the JAR and the library stays off the device.
MenuProject/loadJar.difference: The companion runs the JAR. The device never loads the library class.

MenuProject/loadLibrary.difference: The library manager offers the same sources as the submenu (built-in, Logisim, JAR).

MenuProject/loadLogisim.difference: Mobile copies library circuits into the project. Evolution uses a relative file# reference.

MenuProject/revertAppearance.difference: The action leaves the drawing intact in Evolution d58a61e0, where setDefaultAppearance has been commented out since 6dce9c7f8. Mobile restores the default appearance.

MenuSimulate/assemblyWindow.difference: When the register value is undefined, Evolution keeps the previous highlight. Mobile clears the highlight and reports the undefined value. Evolution updates the highlight on Refresh, on register selection, or while ticks are enabled. Mobile follows the value at every simulation step.
MenuSimulate/assemblyWindow.note: The same line was highlighted across 389 states of 4 counters (8 to 32 bits) in an .lss listing covering all cases in the Evolution pattern.

MenuSimulate/log.difference: Logged values match. Evolution starts with the clock, pins, and loggable components selected. Mobile starts with an empty selection.

MenuSimulate/reset.note: The Portuguese label is "Reiniciar"; Evolution's gui_pt simulateResetItem reads "Desabilitar simulação", which does not describe a reset (W2-09).

MenuSimulate/runToggle.note: SAP-1 runs, pauses, and shows 08 as in Evolution.

MenuSimulate/simulateVhdlEnable.note: The companion simulates each component individually, with no global toggle.
MenuSimulate/simulateVhdlEnable.difference: Evolution enables VHDL simulation globally in QuestaSim (out of scope). Mobile simulates each component through the companion.

MenuSimulate/tickFreq.difference: The saved document value matches. Mobile's menu offers 1 to 64 Hz and the options panel accepts any positive frequency.

MenuSimulate/ticksEnabled.note: Mobile uses whole milliseconds for the period (16 ms at 64 Hz). Evolution uses 15.625 ms.

Soc/Rv32imRiscV.note: 288 RV32 register vectors and the full 22-step program through the runtime and simulator.

Soc/SocBus.note: Transactions in the 22-step RV32 and Nios II programs through the runtime and simulator.

Soc/SocMemory.note: RAM reads and writes in the 22-step RV32 and Nios II programs through the runtime and simulator.

Soc/SocVga.note: Mode, size, and all displayed pixels after word, halfword, and byte writes, mode changes, and accesses with no response.

TTL/Ttl74245.note: Physical pins and combinational vectors, including unknown and error inputs.

TTL/Ttl74299.note: Physical pins and 512 sequential changes with output feedback.

TTL/Ttl7447.note: Physical pins and combinational vectors, including unknown and error inputs.

TTL/Ttl74640.note: Physical pins and combinational vectors, including unknown and error inputs.

WindowMenu/close.difference: Mobile closes the workspace window with the draft saved. Evolution asks whether to save.

WindowMenu/explorer.difference: Mobile has a side explorer button on wide screens. Evolution toggles the project pane.

WindowMenu/toolbar.note: Mobile controls toolbar placement through a preference.
WindowMenu/toolbar.difference: Mobile controls toolbar placement, including hidden, through a preference. The Evolution menu toggles between north and hidden.

Wiring/Clock.FACTORY.note: Geometry (terminals, widths, directions, and bounds) matches in all tested directions for classic and NewPins appearances. The clock drives the SAP-1 corpus.

Wiring/Constant.FACTORY.note: Geometry (terminals, widths, directions, and bounds) matches in all tested directions at widths of 1, 8, and 64. The comparison covers geometry only because the component value has no dedicated oracle.

Wiring/DoNotConnect.note: Geometry (terminals, widths, directions, and bounds) matches in all tested directions with default settings. The comparison covers geometry only because the component value has no dedicated oracle.

Wiring/Ground.note: Geometry (terminals, widths, directions, and bounds) matches in all tested directions at widths of 1, 8, and 64. The comparison covers geometry only because the component value has no dedicated oracle.

Wiring/Pin.FACTORY.note: Pins are read and driven in every corpus record.

Wiring/Power.note: Geometry (terminals, widths, directions, and bounds) matches in all tested directions at widths of 1, 8, and 64. The comparison covers geometry only because the component value has no dedicated oracle.

Wiring/PowerOnReset.FACTORY.note: Geometry (terminals, widths, directions, and bounds) matches in all tested directions for 3 sizes. The comparison covers geometry only because the component value has no dedicated oracle.

Wiring/Probe.FACTORY.note: Geometry (terminals, widths, directions, and bounds) matches in all tested directions for classic and NewPins appearances. The comparison covers geometry only because the component value has no dedicated oracle.

Wiring/PullResistor.FACTORY.note: Geometry (terminals, widths, directions, and bounds) matches in all 4 tested directions. The comparison covers geometry only because the component value has no dedicated oracle.

Wiring/SplitterFactory.instance.note: Geometry (terminals, widths, directions, and bounds) matches in all tested directions, across 36 appearance and fan-out variants. The SAP-1 corpus includes 4 splitters.

Wiring/Tunnel.FACTORY.note: Geometry (terminals, widths, directions, and bounds) matches in all tested directions and with 3 labels. The SAP-1 and subcircuit-ripple corpora include 129 tunnels.

behavior/circuit-names-labels.note: The editor rejects the same names as SyntaxChecker under Evolution's default VHDL rules. When opening files, it renames invalid names as XmlReader.generateValidVHDLLabel does, using a suffix derived from the text. The original 2.7.1 profile accepts names as entered, without rejection or renaming.

behavior/event-timing.note: 6 temporal fixtures in settle and step modes produced identical records.

cli/clear-prefs.difference: Profile resets agree. Evolution ignores `--clear-prefs` when combined with `-t` and clears all preferences when it applies the reset. Mobile always restores the gate settings, language, and template.

cli/geometry.difference: Evolution positions its main window. The Mobile JVM launcher runs without a window and returns code 2 with a diagnostic. Android and iOS use system geometry.

cli/help.difference: Both exit with code 0 and print usage. Each lists its own options. Mobile help omits `-h`, `-m`, and `--fpga-cable`.

cli/locale.difference: Both persist `en` and `pt` in the same way. Evolution accepts 13 exact language identifiers and rejects `pt-BR`. Mobile supports `en` and `pt`, including regional variants.

cli/new-file-format.difference: Five files, including one from 2.7.1, simulate identically in Evolution after both conversions. Evolution writes `source=5.1.0dev`. Mobile preserves the source version.

cli/no-splash.difference: Both start without a splash screen. Mobile reports on stderr that the JVM launcher has no splash screen.

cli/substitute.difference: Absolute paths behave the same. Mobile resolves relative OLD paths from the project folder and requires an explicit mapping for each `.circ` library. Evolution resolves them from the working directory.

cli/test-circuit.difference: Pass and fail outcomes match. Evolution's `-b` starts QuestaSim and reads an asynchronous simulator on wall-clock time. Mobile uses logical ticks. Failures exit with 255 in Evolution and 1 in Mobile.

cli/test-fpga.difference: HDLONLY on BASYS3 matches for the Vivado flow, pins, I/O standards, and clock. Evolution accepts the board name and writes to `FPGAWorkspace`. Mobile accepts the XML and writes a ZIP using its own generator.

cli/test-vector.difference: Failing vectors, observed values, and totals match. Evolution prints text and exits with 0 even when vectors fail. Mobile prints CSV and exits with 1.

cli/tty.difference: With `-t` or `--tty`, tables, traces with `halt`, `stats`, `speed`, and TTY bytes match. The literal `-tty` retains the Logisim 2.7.1 profile in Mobile.

cli/version.difference: Both exit with code 0. Evolution prints its name, URL, commit, and JVM. Mobile prints `Logisim Mobile <version>`.

format/autosave.difference: Evolution periodically writes `.NOME.circ.autosave` and offers recovery when opening the project. Mobile saves drafts in the workspace, independently of `.circ.autosave` files.

format/blif.difference: Declarations and simulation match in Evolution's dialect. Mobile also accepts `.names` tables and `.latch`, which Evolution's BlifParser rejects or ignores.

format/circ.note: 7 circuits and 222 records, with matching results after reopening the exports in Evolution. Mobile applies the same renaming as Evolution when it opens invalid names and labels (#321). Files from before 4.1.0dev leave #FPArithmetic to repairFloatLibrary (#323). Projects from the original 2.7.1 edition retain unrestricted names.

format/image-gif.note: ImageIO palette (PaletteBuilder). Decoded pixels from Android and iOS rasters match Evolution's GIF in 78/78 regions.

format/image-jpg.difference: The exported drawing matches Evolution in dimensions and all 78 regions. The system JPEG encoder uses quality 90, so its bytes differ from Evolution's ImageIO output.

format/image-svg.note: SVG export supports any circuit. Like Evolution, it uses a complete vector scene when available and otherwise records the canvas.

format/image-wavedrom.difference: Waveforms and data match, with all-zero and all-one buses written as `0` and `1`. Evolution names the bus `q[3..0]` and ends each lane with an `x` sampled past the end.

integration/external-jar.note: The companion runs it in the macOS sandbox. Outputs match Evolution's Loader with the same JAR.

integration/fpga-build.difference: Part, HDL, and constraints match. Mobile's Vivado script uses non-project mode (`build.tcl`). Evolution creates a Vivado project. Running the toolchain is out of scope.

integration/hdl-blif.difference: Declarations and simulation steps match in Evolution's dialect. Mobile also accepts `.names` tables and `.latch`, which Evolution's BlifParser rejects or ignores.

integration/hdl-vhdl.note: Entity, ports, and generics match Evolution's VhdlParser, including generics without values and time generics (fs).

integration/soc-debugger.note: Trace with getAsmInstruction() text and Evolution's RV32 and Nios II assemblers, including .macro/.endm, @1…@N, and local labels (#357).

integration/soc-drivers.difference: Evolution's C driver writes DirectionReg at `base[2]` (0x8), but its PioState decodes direction at 0x4. The driver generates Outset/Outclear only when inputs are present. Mobile follows the bus decoder and uses a different C style.

integration/telnet.difference: Edge-sampled values and socket bytes match, including after a peer reset. Mobile updates dataOut/available on the same edge, closes the old peer when a new connection replaces it, and listens on 127.0.0.1. Evolution listens on 0.0.0.0.

option/simlimit.note: Same propagation cutoff as Evolution (simlimit − 1 steps) for a chain of 12 buffers and an oscillating ring tested with -tty table,halt at 14 limits.

option/simrand.difference: Order-independent settled results match at simrand 0 and 32. Random delays cannot be compared run to run, and Evolution draws from a Random with no explicit seed.
